ai.description: Bibron's Slender Coral Snake (Elapidae) reaches 40–60 cm. It is dark brown to black with thin, pale yellow crossbands and a bright red tail. The head and belly feature distinct black-and-white patterns.
ai.identificationRemarks: Bibron's Coral Snake is best distinguished by the broad, white-edged black bands separated by narrow, bright red or orange rings, and the absence of a distinct nuchal collar.
ai.habitat: Bibron's coral snake inhabits the wet evergreen forests and moist deciduous woodlands of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Bibron's Slender Coral Snake is primarily nocturnal and possesses a defensive habit of curling its tail into a tight coil to expose its bright red underside when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calliophis bibroni* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months in Southern India.
ai.distributionRemarks: Calliophis bibroni is endemic to the Western Ghats of southern India, primarily inhabiting evergreen forests and plantations at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
